answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This holds because a newly minted alias starts worthless, so the attacker must first farm credibility on each one before it can swing a verdict. The practical consequence is a steady economy where reputation is earned slowly, spent carefully, and never inflated by a sudden influx of cheap accounts.
